subject: OptiMed on-ramp: grant request + rate adjustment
messages:
From: Susan Kaplan <susan.kaplan@optimed.com>
To: mina.haddad@redwood.com, procurement@optimed.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Redwood on-ramp: pilot credits + temporary rate request

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at OptiMed is excited about the reduction in triage time your runtime showed. We have two asks as we prepare an accelerated pilot for our clinical ops group: 1) a short on-ramp grant of usage credits to cover initial integration + spike testing, and 2) a temporary introductory rate for the first six months if we commit to rolling Redwood into our production triage flow.

Specifically: could Redwood provide a $25,000 credit (applied to usage) and extend the standard 30-day pilot to 90 days for this work? In exchange we can offer a 12-month minimum commit if we see the expected 50% reduction in triage load. Additionally we're requesting a 25% off list rate for the first six months to help us absorb initial integration costs.

I attached our procurement checklist and the pilot acceptance criteria. Our procurement lead (procurement@optimed.com) is copied. We need an internal approval path on your side to move quickly — target kickoff week of July 12.

Are these concessions you can escalate to leadership? If so, please share the proposed SOW and DocuSign link and I’ll get procurement looped for signatures.

Thanks,
Susan Kaplan
Head of Clinical Ops
OptiMed Solutions
Attachment: OptiMed_procurement_checklist.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Susan Kaplan <susan.kaplan@optimed.com>
Cc: procurement@optimed.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 20:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Redwood on-ramp: pilot credits + temporary rate request

Hi Susan — great to hear the demo landed. Appreciate the clarity on acceptance criteria and timeline.

Short answer: we can do an on-ramp grant plus a pilot extension, but the combination of credits + a 25% introductory discount requires exec sign-off because it’s outside standard commercial playbooks. I’m escalating now and will propose an alternative that meets both sides.

Proposed (subject to exec approval):
- One-time usage credit: $25,000 applied to pilot consumption
- Pilot extension: 90 days (instead of 30)
- Introductory rate: 20% off list for first 6 months (instead of 25%), conditioned on executing a 12-month minimum commitment after pilot success
- Required legal/ procurement items: standard DPA + 30-day payment terms after commit

I’ve attached a draft on-ramp proposal and SOW for you to review. If leadership approves, I’ll send a DocuSign for the SOW and the credit scheduling. Target: I’ll come back with a final response by EOD PT tomorrow.

— Mina
Mina Haddad | Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Attachment: OptiMed_Onramp_Proposal_v1.pdf, SOW_OptiMed_Draft.docx

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 01:22:00 +0000
Subject: FW: OptiMed on-ramp: pilot credits + temporary rate request (exec approval request)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding OptiMed’s ask. Quick summary and recommendation below.

Why this matters: OptiMed is a mid-sized health-tech provider with a sizable clinical ops org (est. 2.5M patient interactions/year). If pilot converts to production we expect ~ $300k ARR in year 1 with expansion potential into analytics. They want an aggressive kickoff (week of July 12). Procurement is ready to sign contingent on concessions.

OptiMed asks: $25k credit + 90-day pilot + 25% off for 6 months.

My recommended concession (balanced):
- Approve $25k one-time on-ramp credit (applied to usage during pilot)
- Approve pilot extension to 90 days
- Approve a 20% introductory service rate for the first 6 months after pilot converts to paid (must execute 12-month minimum commitment)
- Require standard DPA, SOC 2 attestation reference, and Net30 payment terms upon commit

Rationale: credit + extension de-risks their integration; the 20% vs 25% preserves margin while making the economics attractive. We should track pilot health via the acceptance criteria in the attached SOW and include an auto-fallback to list pricing if metrics are not met.

Risk/Ask: This is an exception to our standard discount band, but fits the ‘strategic onramp’ precedent (we’ve done similar once earlier this quarter). Need Marissa’s sign-off for the credit + rate deviation, and Ben to confirm legal/commercial language for the SOW and DocuSign.

Attachments: OptiMed_Onramp_Proposal_v1.pdf, SOW_OptiMed_Draft.docx

Thanks,
— Mina

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 03:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FW: OptiMed on-ramp: pilot credits + temporary rate request (exec approval request)

Mina — thanks for the concise summary. I approve the recommended concession with one additional requirement.

Approved terms (conditional):
- $25,000 one-time on-ramp credit applied during the 90-day pilot
- Pilot period extended to 90 days
- 20% introductory discount for first 6 months post-conversion
- 12-month minimum contractual commitment required for discounted term
- Payment terms: Net30 after conversion

Condition: Legal must confirm the SOW language includes a clear definition of pilot success criteria and an explicit automatic reversion to list pricing if acceptance criteria are not met by pilot close. Ben — please expedite legal review and return redline by EOD PT today so Mina can send the DocuSign.

Mina, you have my sign-off to communicate these terms to OptiMed and to route the final SOW to DocuSign once Ben confirms legal is clear.

— Marissa Cole
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Hi Susan — good news: leadership has approved the on-ramp. Final approved terms below and next steps.

Approved concessions:
- $25,000 one-time usage credit applied to pilot consumption
- Pilot extension to 90 days (kickoff the week of July 12 is fine)
- 20% introductory discount for the first 6 months post-conversion
- 12-month minimum commitment required on conversion; Net30 payment terms

Conditions: Legal will include the explicit pilot acceptance criteria and an auto-fallback to list pricing if criteria are not met. We’ll need the signed SOW and the procurement checklist uploaded to DocuSign before we schedule kickoff.

Next steps: I’m attaching the final proposal and SOW (redlined by legal) — DocuSign link will follow once Ben confirms the redlines are in. Can procurement confirm the party authorized to sign and preferred billing entity so we can populate the SOW?

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

— Mina Haddad
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
